title: Use Both Test Cases
text: A correct pattern must return ['5 star'] for $$review_1$$ and [] for $$review_2$$. Any pattern that returns part of "100 star" does not satisfy the second test case.

title: Testing a Simple Capturing Group
text: What would $$r"([0-5]$$ star)" return from the text "Over $$100$$ star celebrities came on opening night."?

title: Remember Capturing Group Behavior
text: When a regex has a capturing group, re.findall returns only the text inside the parentheses. Without a capturing group, re.findall returns the whole matched substring.

title: Why Option B Is Not Enough
text: The pattern r"\D+[0-5] star" has no capturing group, so it returns the full matched text instead of just the rating. For $$review_1$$, that includes the earlier non-numeric characters before $$5$$ star.

title: Why Options C and D Work
text: Both correct options use a capturing group around $$[0-5]$$ star and require a non-digit boundary before the rating. That prevents $$100$$ star from being treated as a valid $$0$$ star rating.
